Cats by Post
Get closerThe typeFurther afield
The first sketchbook

More room.
More game.

The lovely part fills the screen. You get close enough to see the cats, pan around the room, and keep a few useful things to hand.

Four new directions with smaller, floating controls. And a proper rummage through typefaces with personality.

Move into the room

The first pass used Georgia. This one embeds eleven real font families, so the differences below are the actual letterforms.

Ginger & blue
Next
Plain ×1
Send the post
Leave room
for the room.

The camera is yours.

Zoom and pan the world. The controls stay put, at a readable size. A single action brings the whole room back.

The HUD travels light.

Arrivals, pieces, Send. Everything else appears when it earns its space. Fold the tray to open up the view.

Give it a voice.

Lettering with warmth, ink and a little oddness. More of a game’s title and a postmistress’s tools.

Four smaller ways
to get out of the way.

These explore different objects and positions, with the same close camera. Each has its own starting type pairing. You can then mix the typography independently.

Get closer. Move around.

Camera and interface study using a still of the accepted game artwork. Sending demonstrates HUD states. No puzzle rules or game files are changed.

A more interesting
voice in the room.

Seven display faces, four quieter companions. I checked their designers’ notes, origins and licences, then put the actual fonts into this page. The fit assessments are my judgement; I’m not claiming usage statistics.

The little words matter, too.

All eleven embedded families use the SIL Open Font License. The specimens here contain a reduced Latin character set for a compact, offline sketchbook. Full font licences and copyright notices are included below. Source links open only when you choose them.

Three foundry doors
I’d open next.

The search also went beyond open-source catalogues. These commercial faces are worth a closer look if the game develops its own lettering budget. Their names below use this page’s fonts; use the foundry specimens to see the real designs.

Eskapade

Alisa Nowak · TypeTogether

A Roman/blackletter conversation with much more control than a generic “storybook” face. I’d investigate its text cuts for dialogue and the livelier cuts for chapter names.

Visit the foundry specimen

Escafina

Riley Cran · Lost Type

An upright script with the feeling of a beautifully painted shop sign. A strong route for the title or a tea-room sign; it would need a quieter companion for small controls.

Visit the foundry specimen

New Kansas

Newlyn

A full, expressive development of the Cooper mood. Its softer weights and restrained swashes could make a richer version of the broad, friendly theatre direction.

Visit the foundry specimen

Where I’d push it.

Keep the close camera from the first direction. Try the green fittings from the third, with fewer pieces of permanent paper. The HUD should feel like a few useful things the postmistress set down.

For type, Grenze is the strongest change of voice. Della Respira is the more restrained choice. Gabriela is the small, curious one I’d keep testing.

Grenze has a little
story in its bones.

Gabriela has something
up its sleeve.

The full feature map and the other game modes remain in the first sketchbook. These new sketches concentrate on space, character and typography. The game itself is unchanged.

Cats by Post · Second interface sketchbook · November 2026Existing game art. New, independent HTML sketches. No eyebrow headers.
